historical_citation_inventory.hypotheses_and_discharge: Consumes continuity, absolute irreducibility, oddness, finite ramification, distinct weights, and potential semistability established upstream. Also consumes the standard modular Galois representation with its de Rham property and weight normalization in Pan's modular conclusion.
historical_citation_inventory.conventions: Tate weights {0,-1}, modular weights {0,1-k}; dual cohomological convention reverses both. One-dimensional de Rham twist is finite-order times an integral cyclotomic power.
historical_citation_inventory.translation_justification: Pan v2 Theorem 1.0.4 has no residual-image exception at p=5. The Hom character is de Rham; Conrad local algebraicity over Q5 removes an integral cyclotomic power, and global class field theory gives a finite character. Weights force k=2 and power zero. Twist the form and take its primitive newform. Li supplies Fricke stability of its full coefficient-conjugate span. Shimura constructs the quotient and product Euler factors. Compare the entire Tate module with the direct sum of the conjugate modular representations by Chebotarev and semisimple trace identification, then select the chosen summand. Duality gives the H1 constituent and preserves conductor.

historical_citation_inventory.title: de Rham property and weights
historical_citation_inventory.source_locator: Scholze published 2013, Corollary 1.8 pp.5-6, Theorems 9.1 p.74 and 9.3 p.75, with published 2016 corrigendum; Brinon-Conrad 2009 Theorem 5.2.1 and Propositions 6.3.3,6.3.8; Milne AV v2.00, I Theorem 12.1(a)
historical_citation_inventory.objects_and_maps: Actual Tate representation of A over L′; descend de Rhamness to Q_l and pass to multiplicity summand r_l.
historical_citation_inventory.hypotheses_and_discharge: Smooth proper A, finite local extension; de Rham category closed under summands and finite-extension descent. Hodge multiplicities must be compatible with the B action.
historical_citation_inventory.conventions: Tate module is dual to etale H1 cohomology; cyclotomic weight -1. Each r_l has weights {0,-1}.
historical_citation_inventory.translation_justification: Comparison supplies de Rhamness of the geometric representation; descent and Morita multiplicities are separate standard inputs. Hodge–Tate alone would not imply de Rham.
